messages:
incident-bot: Pager — High error rate observed for aurora-prod (private VPC). Resource: aurora-dedicated-pool-3. Symptoms: 5xx from model endpoints, NLB health checks failing in us-east-1a. Paging oncall: @sarah_oncall :rotating_light:

sarah_oncall: Picking this up. Quick summary? customer impact?

mike_ops: Symptoms: spike in 5xx for requests routed to aurora-dedicated-pool-3 starting ~00:20 UTC. Per-route logs show connection resets to targets, TLS handshake errors. Rolling error graph attached (brief). Affected: ~40% of requests for that tenant, retries currently failing.

alyssa_network: NLB metrics: target group tg-aurora-prod reporting Unhealthy 60% in us-east-1a. NLB connection logs show FIN/RST after TCP handshake from targets. Health check path /_health returning 502 from target. Note: security group sg-aurora-nodes was updated by customer's infra repo at 23:55 UTC (we see a replacement event).

jordan_se: From the SE side we verified the customer's update removed an egress allow rule to the Route53 resolver and S3 endpoints used by our runtime for cert and model config lookups. If nodes can't reach our control plane endpoints or S3 cert metadata, they'll fail TLS renegotiation and health checks will fail.

mike_ops: Logs from a failing node (tail):
```
[00:22:11] TLS handshake failed: tls: failed to verify certificate: x509: certificate signed by unknown authority
[00:22:12] http: read on closed pipe: EOF
curl: (56) Recv failure: Connection reset by peer
```

alyssa_network: NLB-level: connection established to target IP 10.1.24.19 then immediate RST. VPC flow logs show outbound connections to 169.254.169.123 (IMDS) / 100.96.0.10 (customer resolver) being REJECTed. We suspect SG egress block.

ryan_eng: Proposed immediate mitigation (hot path): ask customer to temporarily revert the security group egress to allow outbound TCP 443 to our control-plane IPs and allow UDP/TCP to their Route53 resolver (or set resolver address to AmazonProvidedDNS). If they can't change SG quickly, fallback option: route that tenant to hosted fallback pool while we restore network. This requires a quick rollout: change tenant routing in control plane to aurora-hosted-fallback (5-10 min).

kelly_support: I'm drafting a short message to Aurora ops:
"We're seeing health checks fail due to egress firewall rules in your VPC. Please restore outbound HTTPS (443) to s3 endpoints and our control-plane IPs, and allow DNS to AmazonProvidedDNS (UDP 53) or your resolver. If you need, we can fail traffic to the hosted fallback pool while you make the change. ETA to fix from your side?"

sarah_oncall: Action list now: 
1) @kelly_support send that note to customer and request emergency SG revert (call them).
2) @alyssa_network share the precise control-plane & S3 IPs (and Route53 resolver guidance) in the thread.
3) @mike_ops prepare a runbook to switch routing for tenant -> hosted fallback (steps below).
4) If customer confirms SG revert within 15m, do not failover. If >15m, initiate safe reroute.

alyssa_network: Control-plane CIDR (us-east-1): 3.120.45.0/24, 52.44.210.0/24. S3 endpoints: use VPC endpoint if possible; otherwise allow outbound 443 to S3 (no fixed public IPs). Route53: prefer AmazonProvidedDNS at .2 (VPC resolver). Recommend they add egress:
```
# example aws cli (customer-run):
aws ec2 authorize-security-group-egress --group-id sg-aurora-nodes --protocol tcp --port 443 --cidr 3.120.45.0/24
aws ec2 authorize-security-group-egress --group-id sg-aurora-nodes --protocol udp --port 53 --cidr 100.96.0.10/32
```
Note: if they use shared resolvers, allow their resolver IPs.

mike_ops: Runbook to reroute tenant (control-plane change, <10m):
```
# ops console command (internal):
redwoodctl routes set --tenant aurora --target aurora-hosted-fallback --drain-time 60
# verify: redwoodctl routes status --tenant aurora
# monitor: /dashboards/aurora-routing
```
We will set drain-time 60s to allow in-flight requests to complete.

kelly_support: Aurora replied on phone: "We pushed a hardened SG and didn't realize it blocked resolver and S3. We can revert in ~12 minutes." They asked whether a temporary hosted failover will cause session/token problems — we said tokens are compatible but they may see slight latency change.

sarah_oncall: Given ETA 12m, hold on failover. Steps:
- @alyssa_network will keep watching NLB target health.
- @mike_ops stand by for rollback to hosted fallback if we don't see health restored by +15m.
- @kelly_support keep customer updated every 5m.

(10 minutes pass)

alyssa_network: Update: healthchecks starting to return success in 2 of 3 AZs. Unhealthy count falling from 60% -> 20%. Flow logs show DNS queries now succeeding.

kelly_support: Customer confirms they've rolled back the SG change and added resolver egress. They say they also applied an automated policy that mistakenly removed the VPC endpoint for S3; they restored it.

mike_ops: Confirming application-level client connections are stable. 5xx rate back down to baseline. I'll keep monitoring for 30m.

jordan_se: Postmortem notes to capture:
- Root cause: customer IaC change removed/overwrote egress rules for private nodes, blocking DNS and S3 control-plane access.
- Why it impacted: control-plane cert + model metadata fetch require outbound connectivity; healthchecks relied on successful control-plane calls.
- Short-term mitigation: temporary SG revert, use hosted-fallback failover if needed.
- Long-term: implement preflight gating in our onboarding docs and add a healthcheck that tests resolver+S3 reachability before SG replacement. Also add a runbook for automatic tenant failover and a flag to force-hosted-fallback if SG changes detected.

sarah_oncall: Handoff: I'm available for another 20m then handing to night oncall @sarah_night if any regressions. Close loop items:
- @kelly_support to file customer-facing incident note and confirm post-fix in 24h.
- @alyssa_network add alert rule to detect egress-blocking SG replacements (track replace events + failed resolver flows).
- @mike_ops update internal runbook with the exact redwoodctl steps above.

incident-bot: Incident flagged resolved -> monitoring. #incident-severity P2. :white_check_mark:
